Topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Change

Target audience: University students (Introductory Linear Algebra)

Section: section_1 — Intuition: From Vectors to Transformations

Lecture lines:
Linear transformations move space, keeping origin fixed.
Grid lines remain parallel and evenly spaced.
Basis vector i lands at a new position.
Basis vector j lands at a new position.
Space deforms while origin stays perfectly pinned.

Planned animations:
Show vector v in light blue (#00FFFF).
Morph grid lines to demonstrate linear transformation.
Animate grid transformation using sequential Transforms.

Section: section_2 — The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe

Lecture lines:
Matrices act as compact numerical transformation recipes.
Matrix columns show where i and j land.
First column tracks the landing of i.
Second column tracks the landing of j.
Vectors transform as linear combinations of these columns.

Planned animations:
Display a 2x2 matrix M in white (#FFFFFF).
Show unit vectors i-hat and j-hat.
Animate the transformation of i-hat to M column 1.
Animate the transformation of j-hat to M column 2.

Section: section_3 — Visualizing Operations: Matrix-Vector Multiplication

Lecture lines:
Matrix multiplication applies a transformation to a vector.
The resulting vector shows the transformed location.
Geometric warping maps input points to new coordinates.

Planned animations:
Place a 2x2 matrix next to a vector v.
Animate vector components scaling and adding grid columns.
Show the resulting vector transformed on the grid.

Section: section_4 — Composition: Chaining Transformations

Lecture lines:
Chaining transformations is equivalent to matrix multiplication.
Order matters: rotations before scaling differ by result.
Matrix multiplication is generally non-commutative.

Planned animations:
Show transformation A followed by transformation B.
Display the composite matrix C = B*A.
Animate the net transformation of grid space.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Geometric Significance

Lecture lines:
Matrices are instructions for precise spatial manipulation.
Determinants calculate the factor by which area scales.
Transformation geometry reveals the underlying linear logic.

Planned animations:
Flash key matrix elements in yellow (#FFFF00).
Highlight the geometric connection to the grid.
Fade out all elements to black background.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
